text:
mikayla: heads-up — overnight we saw a large spike in the reprocess queue for EU aggregates, a bunch of shards stuck in RETRY and the dashboard freshness dropped to 6h for some tenants. console shows a flood of small late-event windows + a few heavy delta rebuilds.

jamal: ugh. any obvious root cause? late ingest or fanout storm?

mikayla: looks like a late S3 manifest delivery + one job that hit a hot partition and got retried repeatedly. attaching a quick query result in case useful: `select count(*) from ingest where ts > now() - interval '1 day' and region='eu';` shows +420k late records.

ops-bot: Alert: reprocess-queue-depth/eu > 1000 (auto-created at 2026-03-20T03:12Z) :warning:

sasha: two quick thoughts — 1) route "dashboard-critical" recomputes onto preemptible short-worker pool (fast, best-effort) so freshness is maintained for SLAs, 2) expose an approximate fallback path that computes aggregated counters from KV snapshots rather than full replay. both are tradeoffs.

kevin: agree on routing but need console UX for owners to opt-in. we shouldn't silently change correctness. propose a checkbox / preflight in the console: "Allow approximate fallback for stale dashboards" with estimated staleness and token/time estimate shown.

mikayla: +1 on opt-in. also suggest we add automatic routing rules in the API for small-window recomputes: if window_size < 1h and estimated_tokens < 50k => route to fast-pool. otherwise route to batch-pool.

jamal: careful — we have downstream consumers relying on exact counts (billing, alerts). how do we ensure they don't get wrong numbers? we can mark results with a schema flag `approximate: true` but that ripples.

kevin: yep — console should add metadata on the aggregate tile: "data_quality: approximate|exact" and the telemetry API should emit a boolean flag. dashboard UI can show a subtle pill.

sasha: implementation sketch for routing rule (pseudo):
```
POST /internal/recompute/routing-eval 
{
  "shard": "eu-agg-42",
  "window_minutes": 30,
  "estimated_tokens": 32000,
  "priority_tags": ["dashboard-critical"]
}
// response: route: fast-pool, fallback_variant: approximate-kv, note: "owner-opt-in-required"
```

mikayla: that looks good. operationally we need throttles so a flood of small jobs doesn't evict long-running tenant rebuilds — propose token-bucket per-tenant + global fast-pool capacity cap.

jamal: +1 on token-bucket. also add a safety: if a job has retried > 3 times move it to batch-pool to avoid churn on fast-pool.

kevin: for console preflight, UI should call an internal estimate endpoint before triggering: `/api/console/preflight-recompute?shard=...` returns estimated duration, cost, and a list of compatible fallbacks. show that to user and require explicit confirmation if fallback will be used.

sasha: ops note — telemetry/metrics for this feature: queue depth by pool, percent of recomputes served by fallback, and downstream deltas for a sample set of tenants (to detect regressions).

mikayla: owners to notify: @data-platform, @billing, @dash-team. jamal can you draft a short runbook for emergency rollback if approximate variant causes problems?

jamal: will do. draft will include: how to identify approximate-tagged aggregates, how to re-run exact recompute (api call), and how to invalidate downstream caches.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary route-policy updated (fast-pool routing: enabled for percentage=10) :rocket:

kevin: thanks — let's 1) add preflight endpoint, 2) console checkbox + pill, 3) routing rule + token-bucket, 4) metrics + runbook. planning to roll to 10% then ramp.

mikayla: timeline?

kevin: aiming for prereview PR tomorrow, small canary next week if tests pass.

sasha: I'll prototype approximate-kv codepath this week.

mikayla: great. tagging notes in the ticket: REPRO-467 (recompute routing + approximate fallback). we'll sync in tomorrow standup if needed. :thumbsup:

jamal: added runbook stub to the ticket.

mikayla: thanks all.
